rows.subject: Art
rows.title: Choose My Arts Challenge
outcomes: Use the pupil’s actual work to identify their own strengths and weaknesses. Try or compare feasible arts skills and choose a personal arts-development challenge with a reason. Keep the baseline and pupil’s choice. The challenge must not focus on leadership.

rows.subject: Art
rows.title: Make My Own Action Plan
outcomes: Teach how to connect an arts aim to practical steps, resources, support, times and progress checks. The pupil writes, records or dictates their own action plan and tests whether its steps meet their chosen challenge. Staff may prompt or scribe exactly; they must not write the plan.

rows.subject: Art
rows.title: Try, Record And Refine
outcomes: Teach a useful arts technique or method appropriate to the pupil’s challenge, then undertake real practice. Preserve baseline and changing states before revision, record what was done and adapt the next step. Start a sustained process record. An informal outside view here does not replace the later required review of the challenge.

rows.subject: Art
rows.title: Experience, Review And Share
outcomes: A full Unit 1C deck: prepare focused audience questions, attend an actual arts event or experience as an audience member, review its artistic qualities and creative impact in the pupil’s own words, then actually share the review with another person. Record who received it, how it was shared and the exact evidence location. Label preparation, attendance, review and final sharing distinctly; a draft swap alone is not the completed sharing step. The genuine experience may use programme time beyond this lesson spine.

rows.subject: Art
rows.title: Meet A Practitioner And Trace A Path
outcomes: A full Unit 1D deck: prepare pupil questions, meet arts practitioners and gain first-hand experience through workshops or events, research arts organisations, investigate education AND career pathways, and make an own-words summary of the influence. Keep actual first-hand findings distinct from source research. Read both shared slots; empty slots allow labelled preparation, never invented contact or completion. The genuine encounter may use programme time beyond this lesson spine.

rows.subject: Art
rows.title: Compare The Reviews And Judge Progress
outcomes: Complete a meaningful phase of real arts-challenge practice. Gather someone ELSE’s review of the challenge and the pupil’s own FINAL review, using the aim, actual process, outcomes and outside view. Record the identity or role of the other reviewer and the location of their real review. An adult model or generic checklist tick is not either required review.

rows.subject: Art
rows.title: Plan My Arts Project And Role
outcomes: Begin the separately evidenced Arts leadership unit. Compare practical arts-project options, choose a project and define the pupil’s own leadership role. Teach how to connect the purpose, intended outcomes, people and role. In a group project each pupil identifies their own responsibility. Do not impose a public showing as a Silver requirement.

rows.subject: Art
rows.title: Make The Practical Plan
outcomes: Teach and make a practical plan for the chosen project covering promotion, recruitment, resources, risk and feedback. Use the real scale, people and setting to choose workable arrangements. The pupil makes the choices and records their own plan; no pre-written adult plan or invented receipt, signature or chart quota.

rows.subject: Art
rows.title: Test The Plan With The Team
outcomes: Work with actual collaborators to test a project step or resource, listen to responses, agree roles and resolve a practical issue. Update the pupil’s practical plan and record their own contribution and response to others. This is actual preparation and working with others; rehearsal is labelled rehearsal and is not claimed as project delivery.

rows.subject: Art
rows.title: Lead The Project In Action
outcomes: Deliver the planned arts project or a genuine phase with real participants. Show the pupil’s own leadership, communication, role and decisions, and how they work with others. Preserve actual responses and any safe changes made. A finished group product alone cannot identify the pupil’s contribution.

rows.subject: Art
rows.title: Continue The Project And Adapt
outcomes: Support real project delivery at the scale and time the pupil planned. Teach how to use a genuine issue or response to adapt a task, resource, explanation or role and check its effect with others. Do not invent a second workshop or public event; these two delivery decks can support phases of one project. Keep actual role and collaboration evidence.

rows.subject: Art
rows.title: Work Well With Others
outcomes: Carry out an actual remaining team task or project follow-up. Practise listening, agreeing an action, fulfilling the pupil’s role and checking the result with other people. Connect this new real collaboration to records gathered during preparation and delivery. A fictional disagreement exercise can model a method, but cannot replace working with others.

rows.subject: Art
rows.title: Review My Leadership Project
outcomes: Make the pupil’s own leadership-project review from actual aims, role, practical decisions, delivery, work with others and feedback. Teach how to link a claim to an example and judge achievements and limits. The pupil chooses a reasoned next step. Staff may scribe exact words but must not write the review.

rows.subject: Art
rows.title: Find The Evidence Across Both Units
outcomes: Complete or clarify the pupil’s own project review, then check existing evidence for all nine parts: 1A, 1B, 1C, 1D, 2A, 2B, 2C, 2D and 2E. Keep the two units separately identifiable and every part separately locatable. Check exact file-plus-page/slide/timecode locators and the twenty-file cap. Record genuine gaps and arrange completion; the audit does not teach or fabricate missing activities.

rows.subject: Art
rows.title: Practise The Skill, Session One
outcomes: Work on the chosen skill and record what changed between the first attempt and the last.

rows.subject: Art
rows.title: The Review Frame, Before The Experience
outcomes: Prepare the review frame: the moment, the craft choice, the effect, and who it was for.

rows.subject: Art
rows.title: Choosing A Practitioner, And Saying Why
outcomes: Choose a real artist, craftsperson or practitioner from the approved pack and say why they were chosen.

rows.subject: Art
rows.title: Their Practice, Career, Life And Work
outcomes: Research the chosen real practitioner’s practice, career, life and work, and record where each fact came from.

rows.subject: Art
rows.title: Plan The Skills Share
outcomes: Choose an arts skill and plan a short workshop or presentation for a peer, small group or staff member.

rows.subject: Art
rows.title: Deliver The Skills Share
outcomes: Deliver the planned arts workshop or presentation and capture what the learner did and the feedback received.

rows.subject: Art
rows.title: Review The Share And Find The Evidence
outcomes: Review how well the skills share went against the plan, and locate the genuine evidence for all four Bronze parts.

rows.subject: Art
rows.title: Build With Folded Paper
outcomes: Take part in a distinct paper-sculpture activity: learn safe folds and ways to make paper stand. Keep a record of participation. This is activity two.

rows.subject: Art
rows.title: Test A Join And Compare My Learning
outcomes: Continue paper sculpture with taught joining/stability techniques. Identify what was learnt in both arts activities, using the pupil’s actual work and words. Do not require numerical improvement for Explore.
